what: The movie pick now reads what the ask wants and scores every pick against it. On top of the 2026-10-22 line (pick for me's Match N%, which scores the interests it stored, not the ask): "scary movies from the 90s" is read as horror from 1990 to 1999 (lib/movie-intent.js: genre, mood word, decade, keywords), that goes into the model's prompt instead of the generic genre mix, each row says "Matches 2 of 2 (100%): scary (horror), 1990s" and what missed and why, the closest match comes first, and the picks JSON gives every pick a similarity-score from 0 to 100 worked out from its own genre, year, title and overview; an ask with nothing to match (pick a movie to watch with me) gets null and the reason (tools/movie-intent.test.mjs)
asked: Add a 'similarity-score' field to the movie picks JSON so users can see how closely a pick matches their expressed intent.
show: a movie pick that says how closely each film matches your ask
